# OpenAdapt Blog

> Posts, test results, and how-to notes from the OpenAdapt project. OpenAdapt enters approved information into the systems a team already uses, such as EMRs and payer portals, checks that it saved, and stops for a person when something doesn't match. The engine is open source under the MIT license.

## Posts
- [When the screen says saved and the record disagrees](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/silent-wrong-action/): In our fault test on synthetic data, 72 of 90 runs left the record wrong. A check that trusted the success banner passed 54 of 72 bad saves (75.0%), and one separate read of the record passed 9 of 72 bad saves (12.5%). The 9 misses were one fault, an extra write to a billing table that the read didn't cover. It's a coverage test of a hand-written fault list, not a real-world rate.
- [See a bad save get caught: openadapt quickstart --break-it](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openadapt-quickstart-break-it/): A demo you run on your own computer. A fake clinic app shows a save that its server rejected, OpenAdapt's read of the record finds 0 matching records, and the run stops for a person to check the record.
- [We already run UiPath. Where does OpenAdapt fit?](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openadapt-vs-uipath/): Keep UiPath for the program it runs. OpenAdapt takes the last step of one task: it enters approved data, checks that it saved, and stops on a mismatch.
- [We use Power Automate. Where does OpenAdapt fit?](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openadapt-vs-power-automate/): Keep Power Automate for the work its connectors reach. Add OpenAdapt for the last entry that only happens on screen and needs the saved record checked.
- [API, script, or recorded workflow: how to choose](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openadapt-vs-api/): Call the supported API first, keep a Playwright, Selenium, or AutoHotkey script while its owner watches it, and record a workflow for the screen-only step that others rely on.
- [Two apps, one checked fact: how OpenAdapt hands work between systems](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/record-each-surface-then-compose/): When work crosses two apps, OpenAdapt starts the second one only with a fact the first one saved and checked.
- [The write audit: count the saves your automation didn't check](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/the-write-audit/): How to sort automation runs into correct saves, silent bad saves, unnecessary stops, and safe stops, and how to audit your own saves against the record.
- [OpenEMR field test: compiled replay 19/20 at $0, agent 10/10 at $0.55](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openemr-benchmark/): On the public OpenEMR demo on 2026-07-08, compiled replay saved 19/20 notes at $0 in model fees, and a computer-use agent saved 10/10 at $0.55 a run. The agent had the higher success rate, and compiled replay was 1.8x faster at the median. Measured on openadapt-flow 0.1.0, a pre-v0.2.0 source build.
- [The 500th run: compiled automation vs. computer-use agents](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/the-500th-run/): On the synthetic MockMed app on 2026-07-08, compiled replay passed 100/100 runs at a 4.9 s median and $0 in model fees, and a computer-use agent passed 20/20 at a 37.5 s median and $0.27 a run. Measured on openadapt-flow 0.1.0, a pre-v0.2.0 source build.
- [The one number that drifted was the one that changed](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/the-one-number-that-drifted/): Our website kept a benchmark result for 31 days after its source changed. We found 5 drifted claims and now check each figure against its source in CI.

## Project
- [OpenAdapt](https://openadapt.ai): Main site, with how OpenAdapt works, security and data boundaries, and FAQ

- [Engine source](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-flow): The MIT-licensed engine that builds and runs the automations
